Saul tried to kill him with the spear, then tried to seize him in his house, and Michal helped him escape (1 Sam 19:11-17). - He fled to Samuel at Ramah and Naioth (1 Sam 19:18), and Saul sent messengers to seize him, and they prophesied there, then Saul came himself and prophesied (1 Sam 19). - He made a covenant with Jonathan, who gave him a sign of Saul's hatred of him, and when David was sure that he was trying to kill him, he fled after kissing Jonathan (1 Sam 20). - He fled to Nob, the city of the priests, and ate of the bread of the priests and took the sword of Goliath (1 Sam 21:1-9). - He fled to Gath, a city of the Philistines, and feigned madness, so Achish king of Gath did not seize him (1 Sam 21:10-15). - 400 men joined him, then he went to Moab and left his father and mother there, but he returned to Judah by the guidance of Gad the prophet (1 Sam 22), and Abiathar the priest, who had escaped from the hand of Saul, the killer of the priests, took refuge with him (1 Sam 22:20-23). - He defeated the Philistines and saved Keilah, then left it for Ziph because of Saul's pursuit of him, and he had 600 men with him (1 Sam 23:1-14). - Jonathan renewed the covenant with him, and Saul tried to seize him in the wilderness of Ziph, but an attack by the Philistines made him abandon his pursuit (1 Sam 23:15-28). - He went to En-gedi, and Saul pursued him there, but Saul fell into his hand, and David cut off the skirt of his robe and rebuked him for pursuing him, so Saul was ashamed before him and departed (1 Sam 24). - He asked Nabal for help, and Nabal rebuked his messengers, whereupon David arose to kill him and all his men, but Abigail with her apology and gifts stopped David from the evil, then Nabal died and David married Abigail (1 Sam 25). - Saul continued to pursue him and fell a second time into David's hand, and he took his spear and the cruse of water and rebuked him, so Saul apologized and departed from him (1 Sam 26). - He took refuge with Achish king of Gath, he and his men, and settled in Ziklag and attacked the pagan peoples south of Judah, so Achish thought that he had attacked his own people and trusted him (1 Sam 27). - The Philistines prepared to fight the children of Israel, and the chiefs of the Philistines refused to let David go out with them (1 Sam 29), and they defeated the children of Israel and killed Saul and his sons (1 Sam 31). - David's grief and his lament for Saul and Jonathan (2 Sam 1). - David reigned in Hebron over the tribe of Judah, and Ish-bosheth the son of Saul reigned in Mahanaim over the rest of the tribes (2 Sam 2). - The wars continued between the tribe of Judah and the rest of the tribes and ended after seven years with David reigning over all the tribes, and Abner killed Ish-bosheth, and David recovered Michal (2 Sam 2, 3, 4, 5). - David defeated the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and took their stronghold, and also defeated the Philistines (2 Sam 5). - He moved the ark of the covenant of God to Jerusalem with great honor and tried to build a house for the Lord, but God postponed that so that it would be done by the hand of his son Solomon (2 Sam 6, 7). - His victories over the surrounding peoples followed one after another, namely the Philistines, the Moabites and the Arameans (2 Sam 8). - David's kindness to the descendants of Saul, namely Mephibosheth (2 Sam 9). - The continuing victories of David over the Arameans and the Ammonites (2 Sam 10). - He sinned with the wife of Uriah and then killed him, and Nathan the prophet rebuked him and he repented (2 Sam 11, 12). - Amnon sinned with Tamar his sister, and Absalom killed him and then fled (2 Sam 13). - The return of Absalom and his winning over the people, and David's flight from before him (2 Sam 14, 15). - The frustrating of the counsel of Ahithophel to Absalom, then David's victory, the killing of Absalom and his return to Jerusalem (2 Sam 16, 17, 18, 19). - The quelling of the rebellion of Sheba the son of Bichri against David (2 Sam 20). - David satisfies the Gibeonites, and his successive victories over the Philistines (2 Sam 21). - David's song of victory and the list of his heroes (2 Sam 22, 23). - David's sin of numbering the people, God's plague of pestilence and its stopping, and the offering of the sacrifice on the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite (2 Sam 24). - David's old age and Adonijah's attempt to make himself king, then David's making Solomon king, Solomon's killing of Adonijah, and the death of David (1 Kgs 1, 2). David as a type of Christ: David is a type of Christ in many matters in his life, among them:
1- David, the meaning of whose name is the beloved, and Christ is the beloved of the Father (Eph 1:6).
2- David was handsome, ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and Christ is fairer than the children of men.
3- David was from Bethlehem, and Christ likewise was born in Bethlehem.

4- David was anointed secretly, and at the same time Saul was reigning openly over the kingdom, just as Christ reigns secretly in the hearts of those who believe in Him, while the power of Satan, who dominates the world, and his evils appear.
5- David is the anointed of the Lord, whom Samuel anointed, and Christ was anointed by the coming of the Holy Spirit upon Him in the Jordan River.
6- David was the youngest, neglected son, and Christ was born in humility in a manger of oxen.
7- David was the faithful shepherd who redeemed his sheep when he killed the lion and the bear, and Christ is the Good Shepherd who laid down His life for His sheep by His death on the Cross.

8- David went to ask about his brothers in the war, and Christ became incarnate to visit His brothers, the children of men, and redeem them. And as David endured the reproaches of his brothers, Christ endured the opposition and reproaches of the Jews.
9- David killed Goliath the giant who reproached the people of God, and Christ bound Satan, who wars against the children of God.
10- The women cheered and sang for David after his victory over Goliath, and we praise Christ our Savior at all times.
11- David lived hunted by Saul, with no place in which to settle, and Christ lived detached, having nowhere to lay His head.
12- David became king at the age of 30 years, just as Christ began His ministry at thirty years of age.
13- David united the tribe of Judah with the rest of the tribes to be one kingdom, just as Christ united the Jews with the Gentiles in one faith.

14- The distressed and the persecuted gathered around David, and he made them an army, and sinners and the weary gathered around Christ, and He turned them into an army of believers who conquer Satan by His power.

15- David did good to the Ziphites, but they betrayed him and tried to hand him over to Saul, and Christ did good to Judas Iscariot and to the Jews whom He healed and fed, but they betrayed Him and crucified Him.
16- Ish-bosheth, together with the rest of the tribes, rose up against David, and so also the whole world rose up against Christ and crucified Him.
17- Just as David reigned over the tribe of Judah and then over the rest of the tribes, so Christ reigned in Jerusalem and then Judea and Samaria and to the ends of the earth.

18- The warriors who suffered with David during his pursuit by Saul were glorified with him when he reigned and became the heroes of his war. So whoever endures sufferings for the sake of Christ on earth is glorified in the Kingdom of Heaven.
